Module 1: Poor Personal Hygiene & Staff.Description: Meat-slicing operators and kitchen staff perform full 20-second handwashing coverage (fingers, forearms, wrists) at required intervals and task transitions.
Front-of-house servers utilize dedicated clean utensils when replenishing raw meat tubs to customer tables; zero bare-hand contact observed.
Strict execution of a 20-second hand sanitization sequence when service staff transition from clearing dirty tables to delivering fresh food batches.
Handwashing sinks in both kitchen and buffet line zones are completely unobstructed, with continuous water, liquid antibacterial soap, and single-use paper towels.
Kitchen prep handlers wear clean uniforms donned on-site; protective work aprons are removed completely before entering restrooms or taking outdoor breaks.
Staff operating mechanical frozen meat slicers wear clean, stainless-steel cut-resistant mesh gloves covered entirely by a fresh disposable food-grade plastic glove.
Pasig City Health Department Health Certificates (backed by original receipts and medical clearance data) are compiled on-site for 100% of personnel.
Kitchen crew wear clean hairnets that completely enclose all head hair; front-of-house staff maintain securely tied-back hair arrays.
Fingernails are trimmed short, clean, and free of any polish or enhancements; zero jewelry, wristwatches, or body piercings worn on lines (wedding band excepted).
High-visibility, permanent physical handwashing reminder signs or directional placards are mounted directly above all designated hand sink arrays.

Module 2: Meat Prep Stations & Mechanica.Description: Commercial frozen meat slicers are completely broken down, deep cleaned, and sanitized three times daily (e.g., Pre-AM open, 2:30 PM-3:30 PM mid-day gap, and PM close).
Slicing operators execute an online 2-minute Clean-In-Place (CIP) surface wipe-down of exposed blade faces and carriage tracks every 2 hours of active shifts.
Slicing station prep tables and cutting boards are strictly dedicated to raw meats; no ready-to-eat (RTE) side dishes or banchan touch these fields.
Meat marination process is conducted entirely inside functional commercial refrigeration units running at <= 41°F (5°C).
Batch sizes during slicing and marination are tightly controlled; raw meat never sits out on ambient prep tables over 30 minutes.
Meat tubs and storage bins are food-grade, covered, and clearly labeled with meat type, supplier lot tag, marinade date, and exact expiration shift.
Staff never mix fresh batches of marinated meat with older, remaining batches in the replenishment tubs (Strictly no top-filling).

Module 3: Bulk Thawing & Temperature Con.Description: Bulk boxes of frozen pork belly and beef brisket are thawed exclusively inside dedicated upright chillers (<= 38°F / 3.3°C) or under clean running cold water streams.
ABSOLUTELY NO meat is observed thawing at ambient room temperature, on kitchen floors, or in standing warm water pools.
Upright meat holding chillers maintain an ambient air temperature of 38°F (3.3°C) or below; freezers operate at or below 0°F (-17.7°C).
Raw meat storage containers feature functional, unblocked drainage grates so raw protein does not pool in its own purged juices.
Raw meats awaiting buffet or server dispensing are held in active refrigerated display wells or deep ice beds maintaining <= 41°F.
Internal food temperatures of raw proteins and cold buffet items are checked, logged, and verified in LOG-TEMP-01 at strict 4-hour intervals.
Ambient digital thermometers are conspicuous, operational, and accurate across all cold holding and freezing equipment.
Digital stem probe thermometers are calibrated weekly using the physical Ice-Point Method slurry baseline of exactly 32°F (0°C), with logs entered in LOG-CAL-01.

Module 4: Banchan (Side Dish) & Buffet L.Description: Cold banchan items (potato salad, macaroni salad, egg mixtures) held on the open buffet line are maintained at <= 41°F (5°C) via the Active Ice-Bed Method.
Active ice incubator beds are structurally maintained: food pans are nested deeply, ice height matches internal food lines, and meltwater is drained.
Hot banchan items or stews (Tteokbokki, Jjigae, soups) are maintained continuously in chafing/heating units at >= 135°F (57°C).
Buffet service lines are fully equipped with functional, clean sneeze guards protecting food items from customer respiratory droplets.
Each banchan container features a dedicated, long-handled serving utensil; handles are positioned so they never fall into the food.
All raw agricultural produce, fresh lettuce, perilla leaves, and soil-bearing root crops (potatoes) are prepared and washed exclusively within the designated back-of-house vegetable prep sink.
The 3-compartment manual warewashing sink lines and dish pit areas are strictly prohibited from raw material rinsing or agricultural soil removal.

Module 5: Customer Table Operations & Cr.Description: The Multi-Tong Protocol: Every customer table is explicitly provided with distinct, separate tongs for RAW meat vs. COOKED meat.
Table setups feature visible customer signage, clear placemat instructions, or verbal server briefings detailing raw vs. cooked safety.
Tabletop grills are verified as operational and pre-heated properly to ensure meats sear instantly rather than stewing at low temps.
Grill plates are replaced immediately at customer request or systematically when heavy carbonized grease/char builds up.
Cleaned and sanitized replacement grill plates are transported using specialized lifters; clean surfaces never touch soiled zones or aprons.
Wiping cloths used to clean dining table surfaces between seatings never touch the dispensing caps or pouring rims of active customer table sauce containers.

Module 6: Degreasing, Cleanliness, & Equ.Description: Tabletop pull-down exhaust hoods/pipes are visibly clean; absolutely no dripping grease inside the hanging pipes over customer grills.
Dining area and kitchen floors are free of slippery grease films; documented daily application of heavy-duty industrial degreasers.
Manual warewashing lines execute the 3-basin sequence: Sink 1 (Wash + detergent), Sink 2 (Flowing rinse), Sink 3 (Sanitizer immersion for 1 minute).
3-compartment sink sanitizer concentration (Chlorine/Quat) is verified with test strips hourly and logged in LOG-SAN-01.
The internal storage linings, bases, and wall surfaces of all upright and chest freezers are mechanically scraped weekly to achieve 100% 'No Blood Ice' compliance.
Gaskets, handles, and tracks of reach-in upright refrigeration units at server stations are clean, non-sticky, and free of residue or slime.
A standardized comprehensive 'Closing Cleaning Checklist' (LOG-CLN-01) is structurally maintained, executed daily, and verified via supervisor sign-off.
Active food preparation countertops, plating fields, and structural station work surfaces are clean to sight and touch, and chemically sanitized between tasks.
The exterior rims, caps, and pouring mechanisms of all customer table sauce bottles are systematically scrubbed clean of dried residues and sanitized daily.

Module 7: Integrated Pest Management (IP.Description: Zero evidence of active German cockroach, fly, or rodent infestation across dining rooms, server hubs, prep areas, and dish pits.
Internal grease traps are completely sealed airtight with functional gaskets, cleaned on a strict weekly schedule, and free of pest breeding.
Kitchen floor drains are free of organic slime and treated regularly with enzyme-based cleaners to destroy pest food pathways.
Motor housing compartments and compressor zones of all refrigeration units and chest freezers are free of lint, grease, and pest harborages.
All bait stations and pest traps are fully secured, intact, and mapped accurately per the licensed Pest Control Operator schematic map.
Rear kitchen facility exits and screen doors fit flush to the frame; all gaps are strictly below 1/4 inch to block pest entry.
Heavy-duty, overlapping commercial plastic strip curtains are installed across the rear entry portal to act as an active flying insect barrier.
Exhaust canopy hoods, overhead intake systems, and ventilation lines are completely fitted with structural tight-mesh filters/screens.
Food waste scrap bins at server stations are lined with heavy-duty bags, emptied at high frequency, and kept tightly covered when not in active use.

Module 8: Traceability & Water Quality I.Description: Legal Chain of Custody Archive: Store chronologically files all internal commissary delivery invoices or dispatch slips that explicitly cross-reference the original Master NMIS Certificate Lot Numbers.
Commercial tube or crushed ice is sourced exclusively from a licensed supplier; a photocopy of the supplier's Annual Water Potability Test Certificate is archived on-site.
Incoming ice plant delivery sacks are inspected daily at arrival to verify that packaging seals are entirely intact, free of debris, and logged in LOG-WATER-01.
Mechanical backflow prevention assemblies (vacuum breakers) are installed and fully operational on all high-pressure kitchen pre-rinse lines.
Main facility potable water line supply test records are updated annually via a DOH-accredited laboratory analysis and filed for immediate inspection.
